title: The Long Delay to Arithmetic Generalization
abstract: arXiv:2604.13082v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models today still make mistakes on multi-digit arithmetic when they do not have tools, and part of the reason is how numbers are split into tokens. Arithmetic is also a setting where the correct answer to every input and the algorithm that produces it are already known, so training transformers on it lets us study what they learn against a ground truth. These models often fit their training set long before they generalize to held-out inputs, and this delay, known as grokking, decreases as the training set grows. But, how does the representation of numbers change the amount of data a transformer needs to generalize? We study one-step Collatz prediction, in which a transformer reads the digits of an integer in a chosen base and outputs the digits of the next term in its Collatz sequence. translated_abstract: 当今的大型语言模型在没有工具辅助的情况下，在多位数算术上仍会出错，部分原因在于数字被切分为词元的方式。算术同时也是一个特殊场景：每个输入的正确答案以及产生该答案的算法都已被知晓，因此在算术任务上训练Transformer，使我们能够对照真实标准来研究模型究竟学到了什么。这些模型往往在泛化到保留输入之前很久就已经拟合了训练集，这种延迟被称为“顿悟”，且随着训练集规模的增大而减小。但问题在于，数字的表示方式会如何改变Transformer泛化所需的数据量？我们研究了一步Collatz预测任务：Transformer以选定的进制读取一个整数的各位数字，并输出其Collatz序列下一项的数字。我们发现，这种漫长的延迟仅在训练集中不同整数较少时才出现，并且数字的进制决定了……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过一步Collatz预测任务发现，Transformer算术泛化中的“顿悟”延迟仅在训练集包含较少不同整数时出现，且数字的进制表示决定了泛化所需的数据量。
en_tdlr: Using one-step Collatz prediction, this paper finds that the grokking delay in arithmetic generalization only appears when the training set contains few distinct integers, and the numeral base determines how much data a transformer needs to generalize.
